Playbook.name: Windows — Signed Binary Proxy Execution (LOLBin) - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Defense Evasion / Signed Binary Proxy Execution

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A signed Windows binary was used to proxy execution - regsvr32 scrobj/remote, rundll32 with a suspicious export, mshta with script, or msiexec from a URL. Triage question: is this defense-evasion proxy execution of attacker code, or legitimate use of these binaries?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: LOLBins run attacker code under a trusted signed binary to bypass application allowlisting and evade detection.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the signed-binary execution proxies attacker code or is legitimate.

Step.name: Confirm the LOLBin command and arguments
Step.Purpose: The arguments reveal proxy-execution intent (remote scriptlet, URL, suspicious export).
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE (cl LIKE "*regsvr32*" AND (cl LIKE "*scrobj*" OR cl LIKE "*/i:http*" OR cl LIKE "*.sct*")) OR (cl LIKE "*mshta*" AND (cl LIKE "*http*" OR cl LIKE "*javascript*" OR cl LIKE "*vbscript*")) OR (cl LIKE "*msiexec*" AND cl LIKE "*http*") OR (cl LIKE "*rundll32*" AND (cl LIKE "*javascript*" OR cl LIKE "*url.dll*openurl*")) | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, user.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: regsvr32 /i:http scrobj.dll (Squiblydoo) and mshta http/javascript are classic proxy-exec. A URL argument to msiexec/mshta fetching remote code is malicious. Legitimate rundll32/regsvr32 use points at local signed DLLs with normal exports.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: A LOLBin fetching/executing remote scriptlets or code (regsvr32 scrobj http, mshta http/javascript, msiexec http).
Node.Result: True Positive (Proxy Execution of Attacker Code - IR)

Node.Condition: Legitimate local use (regsvr32 registering a signed DLL, rundll32 with a normal export) by an installer/admin.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-LOLBIN-CMD, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Legitimate use of the signed binary.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the usage; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Proxy execution of attacker code via a signed binary.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; open IR; capture the fetched code.
Hunt the pattern estate-wide; block the remote source.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A management tool using a LOLBin pattern by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
